messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 tail latency spike detected in us-west-2 for /v1/stream (svc=inference-runtime). p95 480ms -> 1.2s, p99 1.8s -> 5.6s, error-rate +3%. Streaming stalls observed. Paging to eng-sre.
sam (oncall): ack. I'm on it. any customer-facing pages/SEVs yet? @ops-bot can you dump recent grafana links?
ops-bot: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/streaming-latency?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2
maria: seeing correlated metric: kv_cache_evictions/sec spike ~x8 starting 6543219800. slab_free dropped, prefill_hit_ratio down 30%. looks like fragmentation + eviction wave.
ajay: confirm traces: majority of heavy tails show long wait on predecode /kv-prefill wait queue. decode workers aren't the bottleneck but prefill queues back up and stall streaming frames.
sam (oncall): ok hypothesis: prefill vs decode imbalance causing head-of-line blocking in streaming path. customers hitting long tails. any immediate mitigations we can flip? route, scale, or config?
lee: can replicate on a staging shard with load generator hitting long contexts. I can try bumping prefill concurrency down to favor decode and see impact.
tina: customer impact: a couple of B2B customers report slow chat responses; support ticket #19324 increased. No full outages but degraded UX. SLA risk if persists.
sam (oncall): prioritize quick mitigations: 1) disable aggressive prefill for long-context models 2) increase KV slab allocation on nodes 3) route small percentage traffic to us-east-1 as fallback. Who can do 1&2 quickly?
maria: I can push prefill toggle to 0.5x for models with context>8k. patch config in k8s configmap and roll canary. command:
```
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/inference-config PREFILL_MULTIPLIER=0.5 --record
```
expect ~30s to rollout on canary pool.
ajay: I'll prepare a force-slab-grow on affected nodes (scale policy) and watch eviction rate. CLI:
```
infractl node adjust-slab --region us-west-2 --pool streaming --delta +20%
```
lee: routing: I can add a temporary routing rule to shift 10% of requests to us-east-1 for models flagged with streaming=true. pushing now.
ops-bot: routing change initiated: rule id r-2026x. livetraffic copy started.
sam (oncall): good. Maria, after canary, roll to 50% then full if metrics improve. prioritize p99 and streaming stall counts. set alerts to silence noisy alarms but keep escalation for >10% tail breach.
maria: canary done. initial effect: p95 -> 420ms, p99 -> 1.1s on canary nodes. eviction/sec down ~40% on canary. pushing to 50%.
ajay: slab grow done for 30% of nodes. eviction/sec decreased and slab_free recovering slowly.
lee: routing 10% -> us-east-1; early sign: overall p99 for global pool reduced by ~15%.
sam (oncall): good. start customer comms: brief note to support + account teams that we saw transient latency due to internal cache fragmentation; mitigation in progress. tina please draft.
tina: drafted msg: "We observed elevated response times in us-west-2 due to internal cache pressure affecting streaming interactions. We've applied mitigations and are monitoring — customers may see improved latency over the next 10-30 minutes. We're following up with root cause and preventive actions." ok to send?
sam (oncall): send to affected accounts list. add incident link and slack thread.
maria: Observability follow-up: capturing KV slab histograms, per-shard prefill queue length, and decode worker utilization. Saving snapshot: s3://redwood-incidents/6543219876/snapshot.json
ajay: root cause unwind so far: an uneven refill policy combined with recent model rollout that increased prefix lengths led to KV cache fragmentation. Prefill tasks for long prefixes were enqueuing and monopolizing decode-affine resources; eviction churn created tail waits for streaming frames.
sam (oncall): action items (short):
- maria: roll prefill multiplier tweaks permanent rollback plan + config to auto-scale prefill concurrency by observed queue depth (P1) — assigned
- ajay: implement slab auto-grow heuristics and smoother eviction policy to avoid waves (P1)
- lee: add routing fallback policy to auto-shift traffic if global p99 > 1s for 5m (P2)
- tina: post incident comms and customer follow-up (P2)
- sam: write incident doc and link perf graphs (P1)

Please update via this thread when tasks finish. handoff at 6543220000 to lee for night coverage.
lee: taking handoff. summary: mitigations deployed, p99 trending down but still above baseline. continuing monitoring, will pick up the longer RCA tasks tomorrow.
sam (oncall): thanks. final note: we need a postmortem that includes load test recreation, prefill vs decode queue redesign, and release gate for model rollouts that increase prefix churn. assigning PM contact: @maria to coordinate.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity reduced from SEV2 -> SEV3 at 6543221400. p99 now 860ms, streaming_stall_count down 78% vs peak.
lee: acknowledged. I'll post a short summary in #incidents and link this thread, plus the snapshot location.
ops-bot: archived metrics: https://grafana.redwood/d/snapshot/6543219876
maria: saving config diffs and canary logs to the incident folder. will start RCA draft.
ajay: scheduling a follow-up postmortem sync tomorrow 0900 PT. invite sent.
lee: handing off to oncall-EU at 6543221600. leaving notes in PagerDuty. good job team :thumbsup:
